q: When you create this kind of videoless vlog, where you don't have the video recorded on a camcorder, you have to be more conscious of the story you want to tell.
2006, Stephanie Cottrell Bryant, Videoblogging for Dummies, page 83:
I like to take walks when I'm having my breaks at work, and then I vlog my walks and put them online. I can just ramble on about philosophy, or whatever.
2005 September 10, “Vloggers get political in Norway”, in BBC Online:

In connection to the course and Phd work I've put up a rudimentary 'research blog' called www.networkedstorytelling.org - from that site you can check out the course (which is in English, and you can still apply) and also a vlogumentary called "passage" which I'm in the process of setting up.
2006 March 3, Kristoffer Gansing, “[videoblogging] networked storytelling launch”, in Videoblogging (Usenet):
Team Natural: A vlogumentary on natural hair. 31 August 2016.

e: Regarded by the English Dialect Dictionary as a dialectal form of flother; see that entry for more.
q: "What, in the fiend's name, be the meaning of all this vlother? " peevishly exclaimed the miller, though still keeping his voice within the prescribed pitch […]
1839, Windshaw, The Wizard of Windhsaw, a Tale of the Seventeenth Century, page 204:
"'Od's nonsense and vlother! How did he account for 't ? Cows short o' water, I'll be bound. Thic be a likely tale, when we gets short milk, an' poor milk, skimmed to death.[…]"
1912, W. H. Kersey, The Darksome Maids of Bagleere: A Somerset Tale, page 166:

Zecond thing: what 'st think volk 'ud want to bide and hark to such vlother vor! Hear enough o't daylight, I count, 'thouse buttowling about down round there, darkynight, a-gaping at a stage! Thee bissen gwain thee ownzelf, bist, Farmer?" "I gwain!" said Farmer Boggis."
1922, Samuel Robinson Littlewood, Somerset and the Drama, page 89:
[…] all of a vlother; 'e couldn' get no sleep 'count of its hollerings and carryings on.[…]

Blend of vlog + apology. Popularised in a January 2020 study of YouTuber apology videos by data visualisation website The Pudding, but attested earlier (see quotations).
q: fucking RUINED this guy myers needs a vlogpology without hte^([sic]) mask ...SHOW YOURSELF MYERS !
2013 April 10, JMMA_ALLDAY, Twitter:
And this is what he was trying to do. A vlog apology. Vlogpology. 👌
2017 March 7, InTechTodayPod, Twitter:
vlogpology (noun): when a famous YouTuber becomes embroiled in a controversy, makes headlines, and releases an apology video.
2020 January, Arjun Kakkar, Russell Samora, “The Aftermath of a YouTube Apology”, in The Pudding:

My findings also show that vlogpologies are often created when the vlogger is under extreme duress and may be uncomfortable with being told to apologise, which can result in non-apologetic language and seem insincere.
